user.title: Proxon Control
user.description: How should Home Assistant reach your Proxon unit?

menu_options.direct: Log in with Device ID + password (home network and/or Proxon server)

direct.title: Log in with Device ID + password
direct.description:
The same login as in the Proxon Control app: your appliance's Device ID and password.

Home Assistant can talk to the unit directly in your home network (fast, works without internet) and use the Proxon server as a fallback. On the first connection a certificate is fetched once from the Proxon portal; the unit must have been online at least once since.

data_description.mode: Home network first: fastest, the Proxon server is only used when the unit can't be reached directly.
data_description.local_host: Leave empty to find the unit automatically. Enter its address if it isn't found (e.g. a different subnet or VLAN); a fixed address in the router helps.

local.title: Log in with Device ID + password (home network)
local.description:
The same login as in the Proxon Control app: your appliance's Device ID and password.

On this system (for example a Raspberry Pi) Home Assistant talks to the unit directly in your home network – Nabto's library for the Proxon server isn't available here. A certificate is fetched once from the Proxon portal; the unit must have been online at least once since. Home Assistant and the unit must be in the same network.

data_description.local_host: Leave empty to find the unit automatically. Enter its address if it isn't found (e.g. a different subnet or VLAN); a fixed address in the router helps.

bridge.title: Proxon Bridge add-on
bridge.description: Address and port of the Proxon Bridge (port 8765 by default) – the add-on on this Home Assistant, or the bridge container on another computer (e.g. a NAS, for Home Assistant on a Raspberry Pi).

data_description.token: Only if the bridge has an access key set (add-on option "token" or PROXON_TOKEN). Leave empty otherwise.

reauth_confirm.title: Log in again
reauth_confirm.description: Enter the password for Device ID {device_id}.

error.invalid_auth: Device ID or password is wrong.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the unit. Check the Device ID and the internet connection.
error.invalid_token: The bridge rejected the access key. Enter the same key as in the bridge.
error.cannot_connect_local: The unit didn't answer in the home network. Check that it is switched on and in the same network, or enter its IP address. Its first contact needs the internet once.

abort.already_configured: This unit is already set up.

level_locked.message: In ECO Comfort mode and during boost ventilation the unit sets the level itself.

room_limit.message: This room can only be set between {low} and {high} °C (the room's own value ± 3 °C).

write_not_accepted.message: The unit did not take over {name}: wanted {wanted}, it reports {actual}.

fan_no_off.message: The ventilation can't be switched off on its own. To switch off the whole unit, set the operating mode to Off.

water_limit.message: The hot water can only be set between {low} and {high} °C.

schedule_no_entry.message: Choose which Proxon unit to use (Proxon Control must be set up and loaded).

schedule_not_loaded.message: The weekly schedule hasn't been read from the unit yet. Try again in a moment.

schedule_end_before_start.message: {day}: phase {phase} must end after it starts ({start}–{end}). Phases across midnight aren't possible.

schedule_overlap.message: {day}: the phases {first} and {second} overlap or touch. Leave at least one minute between them.

schedule_running.message: {day}: phase {phase} ({start}–{end}) is running right now. Only its level (1–4) can be changed until it ends.

schedule_running_margin.message: {day}: phase {phase} is running and starts or ends within 10 minutes. Change it later.

schedule_too_soon.message: {day}: times can only be changed for phases that start at least 2 hours from now (by the unit's clock). Phase {phase} starts sooner.

schedule_clock_unknown.message: {day}: the unit's clock couldn't be read, so times can't be changed safely right now.

holiday_not_ready.message: Holiday mode: not all current values have been read from the unit yet. Try again in a moment.

write_blocked_fault.message: The unit reports a fault ({words}), so "{name}" was not changed. During a fault only switching off, the ventilation level and room temperatures can be changed.

season_limits.message: "Summer above" has to be higher than "winter below" – the gap keeps it from switching back and forth.

init.title: Proxon Control
init.description:
How should Home Assistant reach the unit, and how often should it ask for its values? Over the home network short intervals are no problem; through Proxon's server, shorter times put more load on the connection.

Hot water as a store: choose the sensors for solar surplus and electricity price. Switch the use on and off and set the limits on the Proxon device page.

data_description.mode: Home network first: fastest, the Proxon server is only used when the unit can't be reached directly.
data_description.local_host: Leave empty to find the unit automatically. Enter its address if it isn't found (e.g. a different subnet or VLAN); a fixed address in the router helps.
data_description.surplus_sensor: Power fed into the grid (W or kW), e.g. the grid power of your inverter or smart meter.
data_description.feed_in_negative: Turn on if your sensor shows power fed into the grid as a negative number.
data_description.price_sensor: Current price of a dynamic tariff (ct/kWh, €/kWh or €/MWh), e.g. EPEX Spot, Tibber or Nord Pool.
data_description.picture_theme: Light or dark like the device showing them (automatic), or always light / always dark.

set_schedule_phase.name: Set schedule phase
set_schedule_phase.description: Changes one phase of the unit's weekly ventilation schedule. The unit's rules are checked first: no overlaps, running phases only change their level, times only for phases starting at least 2 hours from now.

config_entry_id.name: Unit
config_entry_id.description: Only needed if more than one Proxon unit is set up.

start.name: Start
start.description: Start time (leave empty to keep it).

end.name: End
end.description: End time (leave empty to keep it). Must be after the start.

level.name: Ventilation level
level.description: 1–4, or 0 to switch the phase off.

copy_schedule_day.name: Copy schedule day
copy_schedule_day.description: Copies the phases of one day to other days (e.g. Monday to Tuesday–Friday). All days are checked first; nothing is written if one of them can't take the copy.

config_entry_id.name: Unit
config_entry_id.description: Only needed if more than one Proxon unit is set up.

target_days.name: Copy to
target_days.description: Days that get the same phases.

create_dashboard.name: Create dashboard
create_dashboard.description: Returns a ready-made dashboard (the whole answer, starting with views:): pictures of the unit, the hot water and the house, the room thermostats and all functions, with this unit's real entity IDs. Paste it under Dashboard → ⋮ → Edit → ⋮ → Raw configuration editor.

config_entry_id.name: Unit
config_entry_id.description: Only needed if more than one Proxon unit is set up.

options.auto: Home network first, Proxon server as fallback

filter_change.title: Proxon: change the filter soon
filter_change.description: The unit's filters are due for a change in about {days} days. After changing them, reset the filter time on the unit or in the Proxon app; this notice then disappears by itself.

unit_fault.title: Proxon: the unit reports a fault
unit_fault.description: The unit reports a fault ({words}). Check the display of the unit or the Proxon app. This notice disappears by itself once the fault is gone.

clock_drift.title: Proxon: The unit's clock is wrong
clock_drift.description: The unit's clock is {direction}{minutes} minutes off Home Assistant's time. The weekly ventilation schedule runs on this clock. Please set the clock at the unit's control panel or in the Proxon app – it can't be set over the network. A common cause: the switch to summer/winter time is turned off at the unit. This notice disappears by itself once the clock is right.

compressor_cycling.title: Proxon: The compressor starts very often
compressor_cycling.description: The compressor has started {starts} times today. An inverter heat pump normally runs long and steadily; switching on and off very often (short-cycling) wears the compressor. Possible causes: dirty filters, too little air flow, settings of the unit. Please keep an eye on it and ask the service if it continues. This notice disappears by itself the next day.
